question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution:
The correct answer is **"learning". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The grammatical structure following **"suboptimal for" **requires a noun or noun phrase to complete the meaning logically and syntactically.
 
• The only option that fits this requirement is **"learning," **which acts as a gerund (a verb ending in -ing that serves as a noun) in this context.
 
• **"Be learnt" **is not appropriate here because it suggests a passive voice construction that does not fit the flow or the structure of the sentence.
 
• **"Learned" **is the past participle of **"learn" **and, without auxiliary verbs to frame it into a passive voice or perfect tense construction, does not fit grammatically after **"suboptimal for."**
 
• **"Learn" **is the base form of the verb and is not grammatically correct in this context because it does not provide the necessary noun form that the sentence structure requires.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Be **learnt would be used in a passive voice construction, which is not applicable here.
 
• **Learned **can function as an adjective (e.g., **"a learned scholar"**) or as the simple past tense and past participle of "learn".
 
 
• Neither use is appropriate for this blank.
 
 
 
• **Learn**, in its base form, typically would not follow prepositions directly to describe purposes or reasons in English; noun forms or gerunds are preferred in such contexts.
